title: Coricancha (Qorikancha), Cusco
summary: Coricancha, the Inca Temple of the Sun in Cusco, was a walled temple complex dedicated to the sun god Inti and other deities, built on a sacred site in the 15th century and attributed to Pachacuti. After the Spanish conquest the Dominican church of Santo Domingo was raised over its walls, which still carry the church.

uncertainty.note: The complex is commonly attributed to Pachacuti (reign 1438-1471); both sources say the exact chronology is unclear and give only the 15th century. End is the present: Inca walls still stand under the church.

as_recorded.value: Pachacuti Inca Yupanqui, the 9th Inca ruler (1438-1471 CE)

when.display: Built 15th century CE; church of Santo Domingo above (consecrated 1654)

where.modern_name: Qorikancha and Santo Domingo, Plazoleta Santo Domingo, Cusco, Peru
where.historical_name: Inti Kancha / Qorikancha, the Temple of the Sun in Cusco, capital of Tawantinsuyu

importance.justification: The most important temple of the Inca capital, and the clearest example of Inca masonry carrying a colonial church.

related.because: Sources commonly attribute the building of the complex to Pachacuti, though the chronology is unclear.

sources.title: City of Cuzco (World Heritage List no. 273)
sources.author: UNESCO World Heritage Centre

reviewer_note: Least sure of the date: both sources only say 15th century and Pachacuti is an attribution. The church consecration year 1654 is Getty CONA only. No model: no wall height or plan dimension was found on an opened page.
